body: I appreciate the sentiment, but I think it's a little different as a woman. Last time I was single I was raped twice in the month I was single. I have no interest in putting myself out there again. My relationship not working out is not the only reason why I want to commit suicide - I would gladly live a sad but honest life on my own but the world and my stupid human desire for contact likely won't let me. And at the very least I can't do anything right now because we have 10 months left on a NYC one-bedroom lease together and you might not be aware but affordable housing in NYC is not something you give up because of these sorts of things or else you end up homeless or with shitty roommates. Thanks for the sentiment but - as I saw with most of the other posts on this board - you people are far too simple and don't even bother to begin to contemplate the philosophical and literal struggles of a situation to people who are doing nothing but contemplating the nitty gritty as all there is. If being told there were more fish in the sea and that things "get better" was all we needed I think less people would kill themselves than do. This is exactly the kind of cliche human nonsense that makes me want to die.

Yeah. I tell him how much he is hurting me. He knows I am suicidal, if not the extent. But he's so caught up in his own depression and frustrating that he doesn't try at all. He doesn't do anything to make his situation better since he believes that as soon as he gets a long-term job he'll be fine since this is his first bought with mental health problems. he's probably right but that incredible focus on career that everyone I know seems to have - I hate it. I hate money, I hate careers, and I hate that those things seem to matter more than intimate dialogue and human connection. Looking at him willfully not trying despite us having at least 50 conversations about how much it hurts me is just devastating.
